utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Good afternoon to all of you. Would you call the case, Registrar. Just call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-04-84-PT, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj, Idriz Balaj, and Lahi Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Would you bring the accused in, someone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: So yes, please. Would you take the, yes, earphones on. This is Mr. Brahimaj. Can you follow the proceedings in a language which you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BRAHIMAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Good. Good afternoon, Mr. Balaj. I should ask you, can you follow the proceedings in a language you understand? Is there translation?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, there is translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Could we hear the appearance for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: My name is Moore, I am a senior trial attorney. I have assisted by my friend Gilles Dutertre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: And for the Defence of Mr. Haradinaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour my name is Ben Emmerson, I appear as lead counsel for Mr. Haradinaj together with Mr. Rod Dixon and Mr. Michael O'Reilly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Welcome to you as well. And for Mr. Balaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Gregor Guy-Smith appearing on behalf of Mr. Balaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: And for Mr. Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Richard Harvey appearing on behalf of Mr. Brahimaj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. And then I think we are all aware of the purpose of this Status Conference as it follows from the name. We are gathered in order to be aware of the status of this case but also to organise exchanges and to ensure that the preparation of this -- Mr. Balaj, can you follow the proceeding now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED BALAJ
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Now, yes, but for and moment it was interrupted. I didn't get any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I was just mentioning that the purpose of this meeting is to be aware of the status -- of the status of the case and to ensure that the preparation of the trial will be as expeditious as possible. Then, of course, we should also give the accused the possibility to raise any issues including the conditions in the -- during their detention. I have been informed that you have had -- the attorneys have had this morning a meeting with the senior legal officer of this Chamber, and I have been of the outcome of this meeting. I have noticed that at present there is no outstanding motions. I am aware that that could change very soon, but that is the present situation. I am also aware that there has been no disclosure according to Rule 66(A)(ii) or 68 from the Prosecutor's side, but I know that this has been discussed, and there seems to be no conflict in this matter. So the work plan, which I understand was discussed during the meeting, the 65 ter meeting this morning, is now -- and there have only been very, very slight changes since the last Status Conference, but there is a possibility, I understand, that this trial could start in November 2006, and the work plan is made to allow for this possibility. I understand that the Prosecution will complete its disclosure according 66(A) by May 2006, and that the disclosure, according to Rule 68 will be ongoing. The Prosecution will propose a list of agreed facts to the Defence by May 2006, and the discussion followed upon this between the parties should be finalised by July 2006. The pre-trial brief from the Prosecution should be in August 2006, and the Defence, similar pre-trial brief in September 2006. The Pre-Trial Conference, according to this plan, should be able to take place in October 2006, and the start of trial, as I mentioned, in November 2006. That is, of course, at this moment only a plan. Nobody knows if that would be possible, but that is at least as it is planned as a possibility. And the length of the trial still is estimated to be roughly around 18 months, but maybe it would be shorter, but nobody expects it to Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. be shorter than 12 months. So that is, I suppose, what was already discussed this morning, and I would like to ask the parties if they wish to raise any other matters before me here this afternoon. The Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOORE
utterances.text: On behalf of the Prosecution, may I raise two matters for the record. The first was discussed already this morning at the 65 ter hearing. It relates to whether there will be an E-Court in existence for this trial. I understand that there are variations and directives being considered on this topic, but clearly from the Prosecution and, I suspect, the Defence standpoint it would be of enormous assistance if we could be informed of this decision as soon as possible. That would be the first matter that we would wish to raise. And the second, again we have discussed it this morning and it is as follows: In respect of disclosure, it is often difficult to know exactly what the issues are going to be for the Defence and the Prosecution perception of Defence topics. I ask and request that the Defence notify of in writing of any topics they feel would be of assistance when it comes to clarifying disclosure topics, and if we can agree some format I suspect that will assist all parties. In relation to the other matters, there are no submission that is we wish to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Good. Thank you. And probably the Defence could answer those questions raised by the Prosecution but also come up with other matters if there are any, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You were, the only matter that I wish to mention relates to the question of disclosure. Certainly so far as Mr. Haradinaj is concerned, the Defence would have no objection to assisting as far as they are able to do so the Prosecution in their disclosure exercise by identifying relevant lines of inquiry. That having been said, however, the obligation is primarily an obligation upon the Prosecution of its own motion to ensure that it has satisfactorily discharged its disclosure obligations and such assistance as the Defence are able to provide, in our submission, should not be understood in any way as undermining or minimising or restricting the Prosecution's overarching obligation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: I'm sure that is the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Beyond that, I have nothing to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes. From prior indication made by Mr. Moore, I believe he understands what his obligations are and has indicated that he is more than happy not only to follow them but will vigorously pursue them. At least that's been his indication so far and I have no reason to believe that he will deviate from that position. I indicated earlier and I'll indicate once again that it is my intension to shortly provide the Prosecution with a letter to assist them in terms of general topics of inquiry that may be not only of assistance to us but also may be of assistance to them so they understand better their case. There has been some suggestion, I will raise it again, that the electronic disclosure system is a panacea for disclosure and the Prosecution's obligation for disclosure. I don't need to repeat what I said earlier today nor shall I, but I wish to put down a marker with regard to the electronic disclosure system, that being that it is extremely important that the Prosecution, when supplying the Defence with disclosure material, if they choose to use this system, which I'm sure they will, that they specifically identify the documents that they place in the system and that there is a comprehensive index which specifically goes to respective teams with regard to disclosure. Otherwise, finding information in the electronic disclosure system is like looking for a needle in a haystack. But I think they're aware of this. If they're not, now they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm sure they are. And it's easy, understandable, what you are requesting, certainly. Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: I adopt what's been said by my colleagues as far as disclosure is concerned. The only other matter I should mention this afternoon, Your Honour, is that we were last before you I indicated that we would be filing a motion for provisional release on behalf of Mr. Brahimaj. There have been some delays with which I need not trouble the Court, but that will be filed today, and it's my understanding from this morning's Status Conference that the Prosecution will then have 14 days within which to respond. I also hope to have the opportunity of speaking with Mr. Rossin, who is of course here in connection with the motion filed on behalf of Mr. Haradinaj. I hope to have a chance at least to speak with him today. I have attempted to communicate by e-mail and that's been one of the things that's delayed us, but hopefully we'll have this matter resolved very shortly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Well, we'll look upon it, course, when it arrives. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: But having taken, of course, those remarks into consideration and marked them, I now want to ask if any of the accused have any matter to raise here today relating to their health or condition of detention. Have you any remarks, any of you? Does -- well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARVEY
utterances.text: And behalf of Mr. Brahimaj, there is nothing we wish to raise today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: Thank you. I think if there are no further remarks that was all. The Court now stands adjourned. Thank you all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BRYDENSHOLT
utterances.text: at 2.49 p.m.
